column1: # TRINIDAD, DEPARTMENT OF FLORES, URUGUAY - the founding nest of the surname.
# Read 13 September 2026 from FamilySearch (Uruguay Baptisms 1750-1900; Uruguay Catholic Church
# Records 1726-2000; Uruguay Civil Registration 1879-2020), searched by BIRTHPLACE rather than
# by surname alone, which is how the mothers' surnames finally surfaced.
# notes/trinidad-flores.md was written from a findmypast result list that gave mothers by FIRST
# NAME ONLY, and it put one family here that does not belong: Luis x Julia, "Emma Liseta" 1876.
# That child is EMMA SIXTA LERENA JUANICO, born and baptised at MONTEVIDEO - our own trunk. The
# note's table therefore held twelve Trinidad children while its prose said eleven. Removing her
# makes the count agree, and severs a link this archive never actually had.
# *** THE MOTHERS ARE THE FINDING. *** Beloqui, Echeverry, Pelaez - these are BASQUE surnames.
# A Lerena kindred marrying Basque women in one small inland town speaks to the archive's open
# question of whether the name is Basque or Extremaduran. It is evidence about the COMMUNITY
# they married into, not about the etymology, and it is recorded as that and nothing more.
